# i18n.tr and i18n.format take their arguments as a struct and format them on
# every target as the interpreter does: each runtime is handed the map keyed by
# field name it always took, and a computed argument is evaluated once
# (testdata/i18n_struct_args.txtar is the code).

sngl test --platform none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   4 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   4 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   4 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import "sngl:i18n"

// i18n.tr and i18n.format take their arguments as a struct whose fields are
// the template's placeholders, and the template as written.
struct Who {
    name  string
    count int
}

component Greeter node {
    var who = Who{name="Ada", count=3}
    var calls = 0

    func next() Who {
        calls = calls + 1
        return who
    }

    func literal() => i18n.format(`Hello, {name}!`, {name=who.name})
    func named() => i18n.format(`{name} has {count, plural, one{# item} other{# items}}`, who)
    func computed() => i18n.format(`{name}:{count}`, next())
    func translated() => i18n.tr(`Hi {name}`, {name="Bo"})
    text(value=literal())
}

func testLiteral(t Test, c Greeter) {
    t.setContext(i18n.locale, "en")
    t.assert(c.literal() == "Hello, Ada!")
}

func testNamedStruct(t Test, c Greeter) {
    t.setContext(i18n.locale, "en")
    t.assert(c.named() == "Ada has 3 items")
}

func testComputedOnce(t Test, c Greeter) {
    t.setContext(i18n.locale, "en")
    t.assert(c.computed() == "Ada:3")
    t.assert(c.calls == 1)
}

func testTranslated(t Test, c Greeter) {
    t.setContext(i18n.locale, "en")
    t.assert(c.translated() == "Hi Bo")
}

window {
    Greeter
}
